target.title: fix(telegram): restore preview tool progress callbacks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram users running preview streaming, including `streaming.mode: "partial"` with `streaming.preview.toolProgress: true`, could stop seeing tool-call progress in live Telegram bubbles even though the config explicitly enabled it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram already suppresses the default durable tool-summary messages when its live draft preview owns tool progress. This change also opts that active Telegram preview lane into the shared dispatcher’s quiet tool-lifecycle callback path, so the channel-owned preview still receives tool starts while the default summaries remain suppressed.

## User Impact

Telegram preview bubbles can show tool-call progress again under the existing partial-preview config. Operators do not need a new config key; the existing `preview.toolProgress` setting is honored by the dispatcher path that was dropping callbacks.

## Evidence

### Summary

- Set `allowToolLifecycleWhenProgressHidden` for Telegram replies when an answer draft stream is active and preview tool progress is enabled.
- Added a regression test for the exact `partial` preview tool-progress configuration so Telegram verifies the shared dispatcher option it passes downstream.

### Root Cause

Live config inspection showed the host Telegram gateway was using `streaming.mode: "partial"`, `streaming.preview.toolProgress: true`, and `streaming.preview.commandText: "raw"`; stored Telegram sessions had reasoning/block streaming unset, so the missing bubbles were not explained by a config-level block/reasoning override. The separate container gateway had a different block-streaming config, but it was not the active Telegram traffic source inspected for this regression.

Code inspection showed Telegram set `suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages` whenever the answer draft stream was active, which is correct because the live preview owns tool progress. The shared dispatcher wrapper only forwards tool lifecycle callbacks while default tool summaries are hidden when the channel sets `allowToolLifecycleWhenProgressHidden`. Discord already uses that contract for channel-owned progress; Telegram did not, so the default summaries were suppressed and Telegram’s preview callback was not forwarded.

### Real behavior proof

Before this patch, the Telegram unit tests exercised `replyOptions.onToolStart` directly inside the Telegram dispatch mock, bypassing the shared dispatcher wrapper that suppresses callbacks when tool summaries are hidden. The new regression test checks the real Telegram-to-dispatch option handoff for `partial` + `preview.toolProgress: true`:

- `suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages` is still `true` so default durable summaries stay suppressed.
- `allowToolLifecycleWhenProgressHidden` is now `true` so the shared dispatcher forwards tool lifecycle events to the Telegram preview path.

Focused test result after the patch:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts -t "quiet tool lifecycle|tool progress" --reporter=verbose
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  8 passed | 162 skipped (170)
```

Shared dispatcher contract check:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts -t "tool lifecycle feedback|suppressed source progress|tool progress callbacks" --reporter=verbose
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  2 passed | 238 skipped (240)
```

### Verification

```text
git diff --check
```

```text
.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local
autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
overall: patch is correct (0.82)
```

### What was not tested

- I did not attach a live Telegram Desktop/Crabbox screenshot or recording for this PR. Live inspection was limited to redacted local gateway/config/session evidence plus code-path proof, then focused unit coverage of the missing dispatcher option.
- I did not run the full Telegram extension suite or full repository checks; validation stayed focused on the Telegram dispatch path and the shared dispatcher callback wrapper.

AI-assisted: yes.
